Short answer (memo-ready):
- If you terminate for convenience, you must give 90 days’ written notice (p.4, §3.2). Termination for convenience “does not relieve Customer of fees accrued through the effective date” (p.11, §7.1). Put simply: you will remain liable for all fees that have accrued up to the contract’s termination effective date — which, when you give notice under §3.2, will be at least the 90‑day notice period — and must pay those amounts.

Exact clause text you can quote in the memo:
- Vendor MSA, page 4, §3.2: "Either party may terminate for convenience upon ninety days written notice."
- Vendor MSA, page 11, §7.1: "Termination for convenience does not relieve Customer of fees accrued through the effective date."

Short explanation / caveats to add to the memo:
- “Fees accrued through the effective date” normally covers (a) unpaid invoices for services already delivered and (b) fees for any service period that extends through the termination effective date (so the 90‑day notice period if you give notice). 
- The clauses you supplied don’t define “fees accrued” or “effective date” in detail. Check the contract’s Definitions, Payment, and Invoicing sections for any specific definitions (e.g., whether accrued fees include committed minimums, prepayments, or cancellation charges).
- If you stop using services without giving the required written notice (i.e., don’t follow §3.2), the vendor may still seek payment under the contract or other remedies for breach.

Suggested next steps (brief):
1. Pull the Definitions section and the Payment/Invoicing/Fees sections and share them (I can review language like “fees,” “effective date,” “invoice/payment terms”).  
2. Reconcile outstanding invoices and forecast fees for the 90‑day notice period so you know the likely amount due.  
3. Consider negotiating a waiver or reduced amount with the vendor before sending notice.

If you want, I can draft a one‑paragraph memo line you can paste into your memo including the two quoted clauses and the short interpretation. Which format do you prefer?
